facts.statement: Plagiophthalmosuchus lived during the Early Jurassic (Early Toarcian) in what is now Whitby, Yorkshire, UK, and Dudelange, Luxembourg.
facts.quote: Plagiophthalmosuchus is an extinct genus of thalattosuchian crocodylomorph from the Early Jurassic (Early Toarcian) Whitby Mudstone Formation of Whitby, Yorkshire, UK, and Dudelange, Luxembourg.

facts.statement: Plagiophthalmosuchus was a small marine predator that fed on fish.
facts.quote: In life, it was a small marine predator that would have fed on fish.

facts.statement: The genus Plagiophthalmosuchus was established in 2020 by Michela Johnson and colleagues, who moved the species gracilirostris from the genus Steneosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2020, Michela Johnson and colleagues reassigned "Steneosaurus" gracilirostris to the new genus Plagiophthalmosuchus, resulting in the new combination Plagiophthalmosuchus gracilirostris.

facts.statement: A 2024 study suggests Plagiophthalmosuchus may belong outside Teleosauroidea as one of the most basal thalattosuchians, contradicting its earlier classification.
facts.quote: A later study in 2024 by Mark Young and colleagues found Plagiophthalmosuchus to be outside of Teleosauroidea, instead as one of the most basal thalattosuchians.

facts.statement: The jaws of Plagiophthalmosuchus were adapted to produce a relatively weak but fast bite.
facts.quote: Additionally, its jaws were adapted for producing a relatively weak but fast bite.

facts.statement: The narrow snout and reduced bite force of Plagiophthalmosuchus minimized water resistance for precise, rapid strikes, while its teeth were suited for gripping rather than crushing.
facts.quote: The narrow snout and reduced bite force would have minimized water resistance and allowed precise, rapid strikes, while the tooth shape was suited for gripping rather than crushing.

facts.statement: Plagiophthalmosuchus lived between 184.2 and 174.7 million years ago during the Toarcian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 174.7 million years ago)
